newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Loans to spur Philippines' Metrobank earnings.
newsitem.headline: Loans to spur Philippines' Metrobank earnings.

text.p: Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co (Metrobank), the Philippines' biggest bank in terms of capital, is seen posting robust profits in 1996 as well as this year, brokers contributing to a Reuters poll said.
The poll of six brokerage houses completed on Friday showed that the bank's 1996 profit would rise 41 percent to an average forecast of 4.95 billion pesos from 3.50 billion pesos in 1995.
In the first nine months of 1996, the bank's net profit rose 39.5 percent to 3.19 billion pesos from 2.29 billion pesos in the same period in 1995.
Metrobank's profit could rise further by 30 percent to 6.42 billion pesos in 1997, the poll showed.

The bank's earnings would be boosted by a buoyant economy as well as a one percentage point cut in reserve requirements that came into effect this month, and another one percentage point cut to be implemented in July, analysts said.
The cuts are expected to provide additional liquidity of 13.4 billion pesos which could be used by banks to meet rising demand for loans, they said.
"A high loan growth picture of roughly 40 percent for Metrobank in 1997 will be supported by a strong upsurge in both the manufacturing and trade sectors," All Asia Securities said in a report.

ING-Barings Securities analyst Kathy Javellana said her forecast included 650 million pesos from the earnings of Metrobank's subsidiaries and affiliates, which include a savings bank, an investment house, insurance units and automotive manufacturing.
The bank's ability to service higher loan demand would also be boosted as it had got fresh equity from an issue of exchangeable notes, analysts said.

The bank issued $150 million, or 4.0 billion pesos, worth of new shares last month to a special purpose offshore company, which in turn issued zero coupon exchangeable notes to institutional investors.
That raised the bank's capital base to 35.0 billion pesos in 1997 from an estimated 31 billion pesos at end-1996, said Conrad Andres, research head of DBP-Daiwa Securities.

"I'm revising my 6.9 billion-peso estimate for 1997 to a higher 7.0 billion pesos," Andres said, since the new figure would translate to at least a 20 percent return on a 35 billion-peso equity. In recent years, the bank posted a return on equity ranging from 20 to 25 percent.
"The beauty of this higher capital base is that it opens a new growth area for Metrobank," Andres said.
It would have the flexibility to fund major privatisation projects on water and power generation, he said. Currently, banks have a single-borrower's limit of 25 percent of their capital.
The bank has a heavy exposure to the manufacturing and trade sectors, which account for 67 percent of its loan portfolio, analysts said.
Following are the net profit forecasts made by six brokerage houses (in million pesos):
Abacus Securities 4,845 5,949
All AsiaSecurities 4,902 6,028
Angping Securities 5,000 7,000
Asia Equity 4,870 6,070
DBP-Daiwa 5,113 7,000
ING-Barings 4,941 6,472
Average 4,945 6,419
